question: What does the idiom 'Go the extra mile' mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "Work harder than expected".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Go the extra mile"** means putting in additional effort beyond what is expected or required. (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना)

 
 
• **Example:** She always goes the extra mile to ensure her clients are happy with her work.
 
 
 
• The correct word here is **"Work harder than expected"**, which aligns with the meaning of the idiom. (अपेक्षा से अधिक मेहनत करना)
 
 
• **Example:** To finish the project on time, the team decided to go the extra mile and worked late nights.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Work half-heartedly** (अधूरे मन से काम करना): Doing something without enthusiasm or dedication.

 
 
• **Example:** He worked half-heartedly on the project, which resulted in poor outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Stay idle** (निष्क्रिय रहना): Not doing anything; remaining inactive.
 
 
• **Example:** Instead of staying idle, she decided to learn a new skill during her free time.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Leave midway** (बीच में छोड़ देना): Abandoning a task or activity before completing it.
 
 
• **Example:** He left midway through the project, causing delays for the entire team.
 
 

50:Tbb5,
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
